Canonical fixtures: fixed repositories with literal expected RFC 8785 overlay bytes and overlay_sha256 for a modification, an addition, a deletion, an executable-bit change and a tracked symlink. Enumeration order: shuffled directory and listing order gives byte-identical overlay bytes and digest. Symlink targets: changing a tracked symlink's target bytes changes overlay_sha256, and the target is never opened.

C4 envelope: egress grant equals the reservation digest's hex, transport grammar refusal, not_armed refused, instructions never in argv, recheck_before_start difference refused, one exec claim across concurrent and restarted launches. Claim order: a launch paths echo that differs from the prepare record in run_id, scratch_path or tree_path, one at a time, and a pi-runner launch with no prepare record, refuse sandbox_launch_input_mismatch before snapshot with no claim record. Built-root check: a prepared tree_path that differs from the built execution-tree root by a trailing slash, a '.' or '..' segment, a repeated slash, a different tree below the right /work/<run_id>/fs/ prefix, or a deeper path below the right root each refuse sandbox_launch_input_mismatch before seed capture and before any claim, and the exact canonical root launches. Each refusal-producing check before the claim, through local scratch provisioning and openshell staging, path-entered, leaves LeaseFlags.exec_claimed false with no claim record, and a new request_id then launches the same reservation; racing launches leave exactly one claim. Each claim_rollback failure (upload confirmed empty, openshell scratch provisioning refused before any byte is stored, chain-start caps re-check, link socket creation) takes the claim and then clears it in one durable write that journals claim_rolled_back, leaving LeaseFlags.exec_claimed false, and a new request_id then launches. An unknown upload, duplicate_binding and an injected crash between claim and chain start each keep the claim, so a new request_id refuses sandbox_launch_exec_claimed and reap settles it. Configuration: trusted_policy.config_sha256 equals Reservation.config_sha256 and the raw-byte SHA-256 of the captured effective configuration. Changing a referenced provider mapping, a threshold, the seat_resource_caps record, a template registry entry, seed_root or any effective seed limit (max_entries, entry_max_bytes, max_bytes) between reserve and launch changes config_sha256 and refuses sandbox_launch_input_mismatch before snapshot, seed capture and any claim. Mutation controls, each of which must fail: claiming before pre_exec, rolling back an unknown upload, and hashing the raw client configuration file.

C5 local caps: a capped parent per reservation with child readback; each missing controller or record field refusing capability_unmet with no target marker; no uncapped path. The §1a cases run on LaneExec's automatic paths: a tmpfs scratch accepted only with memory.max and memory.swap.max read back; ramfs, overlay, NFS, FUSE, btrfs and a magic/mountinfo disagreement refusing; and the execution tree on tmpfs removed before the parent is collected.

C6 lifetime, on an injected clock and a fake coordinator and journal: Success: an attempt runs past ttl_s through confirmed renewals, and the stored Reservation stays byte-identical. Clock boundaries: renewal begins by h + T/3, and an unconfirmed renewal fences exactly at h + 2T/3. Fencing: a renewal timeout, a lost acknowledgement, a rejection, a malformed reply and a lost connection each fence the attempt and kill its process group before h + T, with code sandbox_launch_liveness_lost. Supervisor death: it ends every chain process locally, and the lease lapses on openshell. No overlap: no re-admission of the reservation happens while the workload may run. Other cases: lifetime_exceeded ending the attempt timed_out, budget refusal, and ttl_s below 45 refusing before snapshot. Mutation control: a mutation that swallows a renewal failure fails the test.

C7 bridge, status, cancel, release, reap: bridge loss ending the attempt, cancel only through verified owner identity, release cancelling a live attempt then cleanup_pending, caller-scoped reap of LaneExec state, other inventory invisible.
C8 return: patch cap, masked-path and audit withholding, result.json bound and strictness, withhold predicate, descriptor modes, no raw output in records.

C9 routes: no LANEEXEC_* variable appears in the chain environment, and a remote-inner exit 126 before the hello echo is finished with termination failed_to_start and no paths-specific code. the target-specific Pi template selection, with openshell taking pi-runner.openshell.v1 and local taking pi-runner.local.v1. Each template's argv expands to exactly its frozen form, with relay_endpoint as the single argument 127.0.0.1:17690 and manifest_digest as sha256:<hex>. Naming the other target's template, or a template_sha256 mismatch, refuses before effects. The local link accepts one connection within 120 s, and none ends the attempt with sandbox_launch_bridge_lost. A Pi lane goes through the toolkit shim to agent-toolkit/pi-runner, other executors to agent-harness/implementation, reducer and review units never reaching the site, lane_placement disabled leaving the existing launch unchanged, toolkit_interim refusing local pi-runner.

C10 seed and scratch (x-seed, x-scratch-path). Three outcome classes. A schema-invalid case exits 70 with stdout absent and no effect. A schema-valid seed refusal before the claim is state refused, exit 10, code sandbox_launch_seed_refused with its seed_reason, worker_invocations 0, LeaseFlags.exec_claimed false with no claim record and the staged capture deleted. The openshell provisioning refusal takes the claim and is settled by rollback: claim_rolled_back journaled, LeaseFlags.exec_claimed false, state refused, exit 10, seed_reason scratch_unprovisioned, and a new request_id launches. Schema: a non-null seed for a workload other than pi-runner, and seed.entries 4097 or seed.total_bytes above 67108864 under the default ceilings, are schema-invalid (exit 70, no effect). Manifest: a digest other than seed.manifest_sha256 refuses digest_mismatch with no entry opened. A non-canonical manifest (whitespace, reordered keys, unsorted entries, a trailing newline), a SeedManifest schema violation, a request_id other than the request's, and an entry count or size sum that disagrees with seed.entries or seed.total_bytes each refuse manifest_invalid. A symlinked manifest refuses symlink, and a foreign-owned or group-writable manifest refuses seed_root_untrusted. A manifest of manifest_max_bytes + 1 bytes refuses too_large with at most that many bytes read. 4096 entries with short relpaths are accepted under the default, and a manifest that fits max_entries but not manifest_max_bytes refuses too_large. A request_id ending in .seed.json refuses unsafe_path. Path confinement: in the manifest, an absolute relpath, a '.' or '..' segment, an empty segment, a relpath over 1024 characters and a segment over 255 characters each refuse manifest_invalid, while a 1024-character relpath of 255-character segments is valid. A non-NFC relpath, a duplicate relpath and a relpath that is a prefix directory of another refuse unsafe_path. Symlink refusal: a symlink as the file, as an intermediate directory, as <request_id> and as seed_root each refuse symlink, and a sentinel at the symlink target is never opened. A FIFO or device refuses not_regular_file without blocking. Source ownership: a seed_root owned by another uid, a reader uid that differs from the owner, a seed_root mode other than 0700 and a group-writable ancestor each refuse seed_root_untrusted. Source lifetime: after the LaunchResponse, the manifest and the entry directory are deleted or replaced and status, cancel, release and reap open nothing below seed_root (descriptor trace); a source changed after recheck_before_start has no effect on the attempt. Digest mismatch: one changed byte, and a size wrong in either direction, refuse digest_mismatch. A source file changed after capture refuses source_changed at recheck_before_start, with no claim. Swaps: replacing the manifest, <seed_root>/<request_id> or seed_root, by identity or by content, between capture and recheck_before_start refuses source_changed before the claim. Staging isolation: a barrier-controlled mutation of the source after recheck_before_start leaves the provisioned scratch/ and the upload byte-identical to the captured staging bytes. Size cap: entry_max_bytes and max_bytes exceeded by one at the default, and max_entries, entry_max_bytes, max_bytes and manifest_max_bytes exceeded by one at an operator-lowered value, refuse too_large before the capped bytes are read, and each launches exactly at the cap. Undeclared content: a file under <seed_root>/<request_id> that is not declared is never opened (descriptor trace) and is absent from scratch/ at exec. On both targets scratch/ holds exactly the declared set by tree manifest, and a pre-existing scratch directory is never reused. Binding: launch.references holds exactly one seed entry, role config, with sha256 equal to seed.manifest_sha256 and the declared_root source <request_id>.seed.json. envelope_digest changes when any seed byte, relpath or size changes, and config_sha256 does not change with the seed set. Mode and ownership: scratch/ is a directory owned by the exec uid with mode 0700, its directories 0700, its files 0700 when executable is true and 0600 when it is false or absent, and manifest_sha256 changes with the flag. Image links: each link is created at scratch_path followed by image_path, pointing at image_path, with missing parents 0700; a seed entry at a link path, under it, or as a regular file at an ancestor of it refuses image_link_conflict before the claim; scratch/ holds exactly the declared set plus the links and their parents. A run that modifies a seeded copy changes neither the seed source nor the staged capture, and a new attempt's scratch/ starts from the declared bytes. On local, a root-owned, a LaneExec-uid-owned and a mixed root and LaneExec-uid ancestor chain each launch, and a group-writable, an other-writable, a foreign-owned and a symlinked ancestor each refuse scratch_unprovisioned before the claim, as separate cases. On openshell, path-entered fake-coordinator cases make /, /work or /work/<run_id> non-root-owned, group-writable, other-writable or a symlink, one at a time. Each refuses before storing a byte, takes and rolls back the claim, journals claim_rolled_back, returns seed_reason scratch_unprovisioned and lets a new request_id launch. An unknown provisioning result is uncertain with sandbox_launch_upload_refused and keeps the claim. scratch_path echo: a refused launch carries null. Status queued, running and cancelling and the finished launch carry the same absolute path: on openshell the manifest slot's directory's parent joined with scratch (/work/<attempt_id>/scratch), and on local the bound scratch slot. A LaunchRequest with a scratch member is schema-invalid. The check that a hello naming another scratch directory ends the run is an agent-toolkit test. Mutation controls, each of which must fail: following a symlink in the source, re-reading seed bytes after capture, skipping the size check, dropping the manifest reference from launch.references, opening an entry before the manifest digest check, and uploading from the source instead of the staged capture.

C11 prepare (x-prepare). Values: prepare returns run_id, scratch_path and tree_path before any seed read; on openshell scratch_path is /work/<run_id>/scratch and tree_path is /work/<run_id>/fs followed by snapshot_root, and on local tree_path is snapshot_root. Idempotency: a repeat prepare with the same snapshot_root returns byte-identical values under the same and under a new request_id; a different snapshot_root refuses sandbox_launch_input_mismatch; the same request_id with another body refuses sandbox_launch_refused. Replay (x-prepare.replay), on an injected clock and journal: after an injected timeout (exit 20) and after an injected internal failure (exit 70), the identical request returns the retained settled bytes when settled, with no allocation recreated, and otherwise reads the journal once: a confirmed record settles prepared, a confirmed absence prepares once, and an indeterminate read returns timeout with sandbox_placement_operation_timeout and journals nothing. Clock: now equal to settle_bound and now past it each settle timeout with sandbox_placement_end_reached, exit 20, with a cleanup entry and no journal read; a backward clock (now before the journaled start) and an unreadable start do the same; a restart applies step 3 to each unsettled prepare attempt during lifecycle start-up. A different body under the same request_id refuses sandbox_launch_refused. No replay assigns a second run_id. Refusals, each state refused, exit 10 and no change: after the exec claim, sandbox_launch_exec_claimed; a released reservation and an expired reservation, each sandbox_launch_reservation_unknown; a differing reservation echo, sandbox_launch_reservation_mismatch. Echo: launch and status return the prepared values, the attempt_id equals run_id, and a relaunch after claim_rollback reuses them. Cleanup: release and reap of a prepared, never-launched reservation each remove its prepare record and only the allocations owned by its run_id; an unrelated run_id's directory is untouched. After reap, a fresh request refuses sandbox_launch_reservation_unknown, and a replay of the earlier request_id returns its retained settled bytes without recreating any allocation. Races, each barrier-controlled at the reservation lock: prepare against release and prepare against reap, in both orders, leave either a record that release or reap then removes or a reservation_unknown refusal with no record; an expiry between seed capture and the claim refuses reservation_unknown under the lock with nothing provisioned; two concurrent launches leave exactly one claim, and the loser refuses sandbox_launch_exec_claimed without creating or removing the winner's scratch. Status echo: a finished StatusResponse with a null top-level run_id, scratch_path or tree_path fails the schema, and one whose top-level values differ from the nested launch's is refused by the codec. Mutation controls, each of which must fail: assigning a new run_id on replay, skipping the clock check before the journal read, accepting a prefix-matched tree_path, accepting a launch whose paths differ from the record, and leaving the prepare record after reap.
